what_its_for: Selpercatinib is a cancer medicine used to treat certain types of cancer that have a specific gene change called a 'RET alteration.' It is used for adults and children (age 2 and older) with non-small cell lung cancer, thyroid cancer, or other solid tumors that have spread and have this RET gene change. Your doctor ordered genetic testing to confirm your cancer has this change before starting this medicine.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsules whole with or without food. Do not crush, chew, or open the capsules. If you vomit after taking a dose, do NOT take another dose — just take your next scheduled dose at the regular time. Try to take it at the same times each day to help you remember.
dosing: Your doctor will decide your dose based on your weight and the type of cancer being treated. The most common adult doses are 120 mg or 160 mg taken by mouth TWICE daily (every 12 hours). Children's doses are also based on body weight. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions — never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been LESS than 6 hours since your scheduled time, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it has been MORE than 6 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store selpercatinib capsules at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed and away from moisture, heat, and direct sunlight. Keep this medicine safely out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about proper disposal options.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids (like Tums, Maalox, or Mylanta) within 2 hours before or 2 hours after your dose. Avoid proton pump inhibitors (like omeprazole or pantoprazole) unless your doctor specifically approves them. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as they can increase the level of this medicine in your body. Tell your doctor about ALL other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, because many drugs can interact with selpercatinib. Avoid getting pregnant or fathering a child while on this medicine — use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 week after your last dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: chest pain, shortness of breath, or a fast or irregular heartbeat (signs of heart rhythm problems); sudden severe headache, confusion, vision changes, or seizures (signs of a brain condition called PRES); yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or stomach pain on the right side (signs of liver problems); bleeding that won't stop or unusual bruising; very high blood pressure; severe swelling in your hands, feet, or legs; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
when_it_works: Cancer medicines like selpercatinib work slowly over time. You may not feel different right away. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular scans, blood tests, and check-ups to see how well the medicine is working. It is very important to keep taking this medicine every day as prescribed, even if you feel well, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine can harm an unborn baby. Do not use if pregnant. Women should not breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose. Contraception is required for both men and women of reproductive age during treatment. Children: This medicine is approved for children age 2 and older with certain RET-altered cancers. Dosing is weight-based. Older adults: No special dose changes are needed for older adults, but side effects should be monitored closely. Liver or kidney problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have significant liver problems. Let your doctor know about any organ function issues.
